<reason>CON maintained the decisive proportionality clash: localized pumping harm supports well-specific caps, drought suspensions, and scarcity fees, not a geography-blind ban. PRO never justified banning monitored extraction within recharge except by objecting to commodification itself, while CON plausibly resolved the takings contradiction and showed PRO's public emergency replacement still requires taxpayer-funded standby capacity. PRO's capture and regressive-markup points landed, but were answered as reasons for guardrails rather than prohibition.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side B's Rebuttal 2 distinction between prospective conditions written into new or renewed permits and a retroactive ban extinguishing existing rights, which neutralized PRO's strongest contradiction attack and reframed PRO's abundant-aquifer answer as ideology over aquifer protection.</best_rebuttal>
